name: Shamir
title: Judge in Israel
summary: Shamir was one of the so-called "minor judges" in Israel. He judged Israel for twenty-three years and came from the hill country of Ephraim. Little is known about his life beyond his role as judge.

keyEvents.title: Shamir Becomes Judge in Israel
keyEvents.description: After Tola, Shamir was appointed as judge over Israel. He belonged to the hill country of Ephraim and led the people during a period of relative stability.

keyEvents.title: Shamir Judges for Twenty-Three Years
keyEvents.description: Shamir served as judge over Israel for twenty-three years, indicating a long period of peace and order under his leadership.

keyEvents.title: The Death and Burial of Shamir
keyEvents.description: When Shamir died, he was buried in Shamir, in the hill country of Ephraim. His place of death bears the same name as himself.

keyEvents.title: The Context of the Minor Judges
keyEvents.description: Shamir is part of a series of judges who served Israel between the more well-known judges. These minor judges maintained law and order during periods without major conflicts.
